[WP] After arriving home from a trip abroad, you realise you picked up the wrong suitcase at the airport

Everything fits! I look faaaabulouuuuus! It took weeks, but I don't look like a little girl who fell into her mother's makeup kit anymore. The gaff should arrive any day now, but that just gives me more time to practice my make up.

I wonder if the person who got my case is having fun with the aftershave while strutting around in my business suits.

It had been a few days and it was probably time to unpack. It wasn't even procrastination. It had been a wine tasting. The arrival in that distant land was the uncorking, the time spent in the hotel was an aroma, the restaurants and museums were the first droplets of moisture to touch the lips. And he, of course he was the first mouth full of succulent red ambrosia that coats the tongue in its warm embrace. There hadn't even been time to drink. By the time it was over, by the time I had to meet the airplane, it had been a rush just to find a bucket to spit in.

 

And even then I enjoyed every memory, every drop, as it passed my lips again. It's not easy to find something that inspires love at 67; even less so to touch love itself. My memory had been failing me as of late but lately it had been well on my side. I still remembered the way he smelled. The way his chest vibrated when he spoke. Even the manner in which he held a glass when he drank. There was not a moment that had gone unsavored and I would have had no qualms getting drunk had the airplane not had somewhere else to be.

 

He rushed me to the port, albeit with hesitation. We could not bear to part and even as we each struggled to understand how to input a number into our phones, we had a time of it. Instead he wrote down his cell number for me on a piece of paper and tucked it into my suitcase. We smiled and kissed once more before sending off. At my seat I struggled to place my baggage into the bin. A gentleman offered a hand and, noticing how vulnerable my luggage could be at any moment, removed the numbered paper and tucked it into my purse before it went over my head.

 

A quick zip of the purse, a recline of the chair, and a shut of the eyes and I was back home. And after indulging in those memories for a few days as I put her life back in order, I was ready to call and devote my every moment with him. I went to my suitcase, which is where I last remembered the paper with his number to be, and instantly noticed that the items inside were not like my own. At first I worried about the expensive souvenirs i had bought, which was overtaken by thoughts of the missing paper, which was finally put in perspective when I couldn't find my medication. This was not my suitcase.

 

I couldn't decide what to be more worried about. At least then it was only worry. The medication had helped stabilize my memory, something which it had been wonderful at. Then for a glimpse in time, I remembered where the phone number was. It had been in my wallet! That was enough to anchor me. Now I called up the airline and informed them of the mix up to which they were more than eager to help. I had already missed a dose but at least my routine was only once every three days. The airline let me know that the suitcase was halfway across the world but they would have it back to me within seven days.

 

That wouldn't be too bad. It was my own fault, being too eager to embark and not enough to get a refill to keep at home. But it wouldn't be an issue much longer. With that off my mind, I went to my wallet and reached into the zippered pocket in which the paper lay. But I found nothing. That's right, I had taken it out the day I arrived. It was precisely this that I was trying to prevent, I was afraid that I might end up losing it so I took the paper with the phone number and put it safely away...somewhere.
